Create a production-ready single-file website in one html file.

GOAL
Build a premium event landing page for **“ARTIFACT: Museum Night”** — a ticketed night museum event with ticket selection, but no real payment.

TECH / STRICT
- One html file only.
- HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript only.
- No frameworks.
- No libraries.
- Inline CSS and inline JS.
- Remote images are allowed.
- Must work by opening the file directly in a browser.

DESIGN DIRECTION
Create a visually striking cinematic museum-night website.

The design should feel like:
- luxury museum after dark
- velvet darkness
- golden spotlights
- quiet mystery
- art-house cinema
- premium cultural event

Visual style:
- dark velvet / near-black background
- deep burgundy and midnight navy gradients
- soft spotlight effects
- elegant serif headlines
- modern readable sans-serif body text
- thin gold dividers
- subtle grain/noise overlay using CSS only
- large editorial hero layout
- asymmetric image cards
- glass-like dark panels
- premium ticket cards
- smooth hover states
- scroll reveal animations
- strong typography hierarchy

Color palette:
- Background: `#070506`
- Velvet: `#1a0710`
- Burgundy: `#3a0f1d`
- Midnight navy: `#07111f`
- Gold: `#d6ad60`
- Soft gold: `#f3d79b`
- Ivory text: `#f8efe2`
- Muted text: `#b9a999`
- Panel: `rgba(255, 244, 220, 0.06)`
- Border: `rgba(214, 173, 96, 0.28)`

TYPOGRAPHY
Use CSS font stacks only:
- Headlines: `Georgia`, `Times New Roman`, serif
- Body: `Inter`, `system-ui`, `Segoe UI`, sans-serif

LAYOUT
Single-page landing with sticky navbar and smooth scrolling.

SECTIONS

1. Navbar
- Logo: ARTIFACT
- Links:
  - Program
  - Artists
  - Venue
  - Tickets
  - FAQ
- CTA button: “Get Tickets”
- Active nav state while scrolling
- Mobile responsive menu

2. Hero
- Full cinematic hero section
- Large serif headline:
  “Museum Night, Reimagined”
- Event name:
  “ARTIFACT: Museum Night”
- Date/time/place:
  - 18 October 2026
  - 19:00–02:00
  - The Old Gallery, Warsaw
- CTAs:

3. Concept/Intro (id="concept"): short editorial paragraph about the event philosophy, then 3 feature cards in a grid: "After-Hours Exhibitions", "Live Performances", "Guided Hidden-Room Tours", each with a short description and a simple decorative icon (inline SVG or unicode glyph).
4. Program Timeline (id="program"): vertical timeline with a gold center/side line, 8 entries: 19:00 Doors Open (Main Entrance), 19:30 Curator Welcome (Grand Hall), 20:00 Hidden Collection Tour (East Wing), 21:00 Live Ambient Performance (Sculpture Court), 22:00 Sculpture Hall Projection (Sculpture Hall), 23:00 Artist Talk (Auditorium), 00:00 Midnight Gallery Walk (Main Galleries), 01:00 Closing Sound Session (Rotunda) — each item shows time, title, one-sentence description, and a small location tag pill, alternating left/right layout on desktop collapsing to single column on mobile, each item reveals on scroll.
5. Artists/Speakers (id="artists"): grid of 8 cards, cycling through the 6 provided unsplash urls (gallery,art / exhibition,lights / sculpture,museum / museum,crowd / art,installation / theater,stage), each card has image, name (invent 8 plausible artist/curator names), role (e.g. "Sound Artist", "Chief Curator", "Sculptor", "Light Designer", "Performance Artist", etc.), a one-line teaser, and a "View Details" button that opens an accessible modal (id="artistModal", role="dialog", aria-modal="true") showing large image, name, role, longer bio paragraph, session time, and a close button (✕). Modal must close on ESC key, on backdrop click, and on close button click; focus should move into modal on open. Implement via one shared modal populated by JS from a JS array of artist objects (id, name, role, teaser, bio, time, image).
6. Venue (id="venue"): venue name "The Old Gallery", full address, a paragraph of travel tips, an accessibility notes paragraph (step-free access, accessible restrooms, wheelchair loan at entrance), a parking/public transport paragraph. Include an inline SVG (embedded directly in HTML, viewBox ~400x300) mocking a simple map: a rectangle representing the gallery block labeled "The Old Gallery", a few thin lines representing nearby streets, a circle/icon marker for metro/bus stop labeled "Metro", a marker for the entrance labeled "Entrance", and a dashed/solid gold path line (stroke var(--gold)) connecting the metro marker to the entrance marker.
7. Tickets (id="tickets"): 3 ticket cards in a grid — "Night Pass" €29 (Entry after 19:00, Main exhibition access, Program access); "Curator Pass" €59 with a "Recommended" badge (Everything in Night Pass, Hidden collection tour, Reserved artist talk seating); "Patron Pass" €129 (Everything in Curator Pass, VIP lounge access, Signed event print, Priority entrance). Each card lists features with checkmarks and has a "Select Tier" button (data-tier attribute) that opens a ticket checkout modal (id="ticketModal"). The checkout modal shows: selected tier name + price, a form with attendee full name (required text input), email (required, validated with regex), number of tickets (number input min=1 max=10 default 1), a computed total price (updates live as ticket count changes), a required checkbox "I agree to the terms", and a "Confirm Reservation" submit button. On submit: validate all fields (show inline error messages under invalid fields, do not submit if invalid), on success show a success message inside the modal (or close modal and show a toast) stating reservation confirmed, and trigger a toast notification. No real payment, no backend call — just client-side mock with a fake reservation ID.
8. FAQ (id="faq"): accordion with at least 6 Q&A pairs (use exactly these questions): "Is payment processed on this page?" (answer: no, it's a demo, no real payment), "Can I arrive late?", "Are photos allowed?", "Is the venue accessible?", "Can I change my ticket tier?", "How do I save the event to my calendar?" (mention the Save to Calendar button). Each accordion item toggles open/closed on click of its question header (aria-expanded managed), only relevant answer shown/hidden via max-height or class toggle transition, icon (+ / − or chevron) rotates.
9. Newsletter (id="newsletter"): email input + submit button, inline validation message under the input for invalid/empty email, on valid submit show a toast "Subscribed!" and clear the input, prevent default form submission (no backend).
10. Footer: "ARTIFACT" logo text, short event credit line, 3-4 text-style "social links" (e.g. Instagram, Newsletter, Press — can be # links or mailto), copyright line with current year via JS (e.g. document.write year or innerText set by JS at load), and a small note "Demo landing page — no real ticket purchase."

TOAST SYSTEM: a fixed-position toast container; JS function showToast(message) creates a toast element, auto-dismisses after ~3.5s with fade transition, supports multiple stacked toasts, aria-live="polite" region for accessibility.

Wired to both the hero "Save to Calendar" button and any FAQ mention/other calendar button if present.

SMOOTH SCROLL: all internal nav anchors use scroll-behavior: smooth (CSS html{scroll-behavior:smooth}) plus JS click handlers with e.preventDefault() and el.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'}) accounting for sticky navbar offset (scroll-margin-top on section ids).

RESPONSIVE: mobile breakpoints (~768px and ~480px) collapsing grids to single column, mobile nav menu, adjusted hero font sizes with clamp().

ACCESSIBILITY/POLISH: visible focus states (outline) on all interactive elements, sufficient color contrast for text against dark backgrounds using ivory/soft-gold, buttons have hover and focus-visible states, no console errors (wrap risky code in try/catch where relevant, ensure all referenced IDs exist).

Structure the JS in a single <script> block at the end of body, organized with clear comments per feature (Mobile nav, Active nav on scroll, Scroll reveal, Modals, Accordion, Ticket modal + validation, Newsletter validation, Toasts, ICS generation). Use plain DOM APIs only (querySelector, addEventListener, classList). Ensure the file is complete, self-contained, and valid HTML5."}
